chapter: Wax Records, Broadway shows and Eddie Condon
title: Playing with Erroll Garner and the Cleveland Symphony
summary: Hall worked with Garner in 1953 and describes the Cleveland concert where he alone was miked.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: What's next: upcoming tours, records and plans

blocks.x: "Every Day". But I had been with Errol Garner then. I made Errol Garner's "Misty" (inaudible). I was working there. Oh, in the '50's, I was working with Errol. Hazel Scott, '53, '53 I was with Errol GARNER.
How long were you with him?

I worked with him later, too. Osie (inaudible) Johnson and I, we made the Other Voices album. And I played with the Cleveland Symphony. One of my big moments, at least ten bass players and almost 200 musicians, and Mitch Miller was the conductor. Nat Pierce (had phonetic) made the arrangements because Errol couldn't read; and we were going to play the "Other Voices" arrangement before Errol was going to be presented with the trio and these bass players sounded like pachyderms and the conductor wiped them all out and put a mike on me, in front of 7,000 people. (Laughter) My wife has was asked whether a musician has an orgasm when he's playing. This was it. This was it. I couldn't identify it as such. 7,000 people and all of these ten bass players, cut them out. Just me, right in the middle of the string section. Boy Wow. I was on cloud nine.
I'd have to check it out. It was Sometime in the '50's.
Did you do mostly concerts or clubs or, with Garner, or --
I joined the theater, the Regal Theater in Chicago, and then we went to a club in St. Louis and Akron, Embers, and I was substituting for Leonard Gaston. I told you I went to television school.

So, I got Leonard interested in going to television school and he was working with Errol Garner at the time and it's near graduation with him, so, I said, well, I'll take your job until you finish. But meanwhile, we recorded 'Misty' and recorded, and did all the rest of these things.
